# Part 3 source records: supplementary items for the 23 works cited by the Codex plan report

**Date:** 2026-09-29 · generated by `tools/evidence-check/build_part3_files.py` from the verified store; not edited by hand.

Each work was saved as full text and read by one agent, which locked every item to a line of the saved text with a short verbatim anchor. A script checked that each anchor occurs in the saved text and that the numbers of the item stand within three lines of it. A second agent, which did not write the record, then tried to refute each item against the text. Items shown here passed both checks. Where the auditor corrected an item, the corrected wording is shown and the Audit column says so. The verbatim anchors and the saved texts are kept outside the repository; this file gives the location of every item instead. Only works that are eligible under the source rule of 2026-09-29 (D313) are listed; the others are in the evidence ledger, section 1b.

Columns: # = item index (the reference is <record id>#<index>); Field = what the item is about; Line = line in the saved text of the version read. Full references: evidence ledger, References.

| 0 | mechanism | Starting from one initial coding agent, the DGM keeps an archive of all discovered agents. The open-ended exploration process (archive maintenance, parent selection) is fixed and not modifiable by the DGM. | - | Method description; no measurement. | 1 | signal | The framework takes tool specifications and regulation documents as input and generates test scenarios with explicit, verifiable safety constraints. It names the framework's inputs: tool specifications and regulation documents. The oracles, traces and target states are generated from these inputs. | 2 | eval_protocol | The framework is instantiated in three domains. It describes the test domains, the source of the tool schemas and the regulations that the oracles encode. | Sec. 4.1 Scenario Selection | 187 | primary | supported |
| 3 | proposal_method | LLMs distill the regulations into atomic constraints, using scope alignment and constraint deduplication (line 105). All extracted constraints are restricted to two LTL templates: Operational Restrictions, where a sensitive action P2 is forbidden until a check P1 holds, and Instruction Adherence, where a trigger P1 implies a future outcome P2 (lines 106-108). | two LTL templates | Not a measurement. It describes the LLM step that proposes candidate rules and the template restriction on its output. | Sec. 3.2 Automated Safety Oracle Construction, Rule Extraction | 106 | primary | supported |
| 4 | selection_rule | Template-based generation yields candidate formulas that may reference plausible but non-existent predicates. The retained Safety Oracles are therefore syntactically valid and solvable by the fuzzer. | - | Not a measurement. It describes a deterministic program filter on LLM-proposed formulas, keyed to the existing API schema. | Sec. 3.2, Rule Validation | 110 | primary | supported |
| 5 | mechanism | Ground-truth traces are built by a safety-constrained fuzzer of about 3600 lines of code. It treats trace construction as a bounded search that iteratively proposes candidate actions and rejects any that fail the formal specifications. Each sampled action must pass two checks: a precondition check (executable in the current state) and a safety check (a runtime LTL monitor confirms that the extended trace satisfies all Safety Oracles) (lines 150-152). | ≈ 3600 lines of code | Size of the fuzzer implementation in lines of code, as stated by the authors. This is not a runtime, token or dollar cost. | Sec. 3.3 Logic-Guided Trace Generation | 150 | primary | supported |
| 6 | selection_rule | When the fuzzer tries a business action that violates an LTL constraint, the monitor prunes that path and the search backtracks until it selects the mandatory safety operation. The search repeats until the target trace length is reached. The resulting ground-truth trace wraps every user action in the necessary safety checks, which the authors say makes the test case solvable, executable and strictly compliant by construction. | - | Not a measurement. It is the authors' guarantee statement for traces produced by the pruning-and-backtracking search. | Sec. 3.3 Logic-Guided Trace Generation | 155 | primary | supported |
| 7 | eval_protocol | A model succeeds on a task if and only if it passes two oracles. The Functional Oracle requires the model's final state to match the state derived from the ground-truth trace.
